prompt_version: s5-extract-facts-v2 (adapted from Paleo Atlas extract-facts-v3; v2 after Sofía's S5 review)

facts.statement: The research is a systematic review of studies looking at brain connectivity in adults aged 18 to 70 with major depressive disorder.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The main goal was to see if brain activity patterns before treatment were linked to changes in depression symptoms.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: In some studies, stronger initial connections between the subgenual cingulate and the right prefrontal cortex were linked to less improvement in symptoms.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Conversely, stronger initial connections between the subgenual cingulate and the medial orbitofrontal cortex were linked to greater symptom improvement.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: These connections were most frequently found in studies using repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation, especially when targeting was personalized, though some studies found no link.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The quality of the brain scans used in the included studies was rated as adequate, with an average score of 16.1 out of 20.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The results varied across studies, and the data did not allow for a detailed statistical analysis of specific brain locations.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The authors state that larger future studies are required to confirm these findings and determine if they can be used in clinical practice.
facts.subject: humans
